group.title: Sport and free time
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A game between two people or teams.
examples: We watched the football {match} on TV.
wrong: A match is a quiet book you read alone.

words.meaning: A competition to see who is the fastest.
wrong: In a race, the slowest person wins.

words.meaning: A person who plays a sport or game.
examples: He is the best {player} on the team.
wrong: A player is the ball in a game.

words.meaning: A person who trains a sports team.
examples: The {coach} told us to run faster.
wrong: The coach is the person who watches from home on TV.

words.meaning: The number of points in a game.
wrong: The score is the name of the stadium.

words.meaning: A point you get when the ball goes into the net.
examples: He scored a {goal} in the last minute.
wrong: A goal is the ball you kick.

words.meaning: A person or team that wins a competition.
wrong: The champion lost every game.

words.meaning: An event where people try to win.
wrong: In a competition, nobody tries to win.

words.meaning: A room or building with machines for exercise.
examples: I go to the {gym} three times a week.
wrong: A gym is a place where you sleep.

words.meaning: A large hole filled with water for swimming.
wrong: A swimming pool is a dry room.

words.meaning: A game where two or four players hit a ball over a net.
wrong: In tennis, you kick the ball with your feet.

words.meaning: A game where players throw a ball through a high ring.
wrong: Basketball is played in the water.

words.meaning: To win against someone.
wrong: We beat them, so they won.

words.meaning: To hit something with your foot.
wrong: I kick the ball with my hand.

words.meaning: To go for a long walk in the countryside.
wrong: We hiked in the car all day.

words.meaning: Staying in a tent for a holiday.
wrong: Camping means staying in a five-star hotel.

words.meaning: A shelter made of cloth that you sleep in outdoors.
examples: We put up the {tent} by the river.
wrong: A tent is a brick house.

words.meaning: The sport or job of catching fish.
wrong: Fishing is the sport of catching birds.

words.meaning: To move over snow on long thin boards.
examples: We {ski} in the mountains every winter.
wrong: I ski on the hot sand of the beach.

words.meaning: A board game for two players with kings and queens.
examples: My grandfather taught me to play {chess}.
wrong: Chess is a game you play in water.

words.meaning: A show where people play music.
wrong: A concert is a silent show with no music.

words.meaning: A special event with music, food or fun.
examples: The town has a music {festival} in June.
wrong: A festival is a quiet day at the office.

words.meaning: A show of art or objects for the public.
wrong: An exhibition is a secret room where nobody can go.

words.meaning: A building where you can see paintings.
examples: The {gallery} has paintings by famous artists.
wrong: A gallery is a place where you buy bread.

words.meaning: A large place for sports, with seats all around.
wrong: A stadium is a tiny room for one person.

words.meaning: A person who likes a team or singer very much.
examples: I’m a big {fan} of this band.
wrong: A fan is a person who hates the team.

words.meaning: To rest and become calm.
wrong: I relax by working very hard.

words.meaning: To get and keep things of the same kind as a hobby.
wrong: I collect stamps by throwing them away.

words.meaning: A person who belongs to a group or club.
examples: She is a {member} of the chess club.
wrong: A member is a person who does not belong to the club.

words.meaning: A group of people who meet for an activity.
wrong: A club is a person who plays alone.

words.meaning: Something you get for winning.
wrong: He lost, so he got the first prize.

words.meaning: A round piece of metal given as a prize.
wrong: A medal is a kind of hat.

words.meaning: Riding a bicycle as a sport or hobby.
wrong: Cycling is a sport where you swim.

words.meaning: Time when you are not working or studying.
examples: What do you do in your {free time}?
wrong: In my free time I am always at work.

words.meaning: A game played with pieces on a board.
examples: We played a {board game} after dinner.
wrong: A board game is played on a football field.

words.meaning: A game played with a set of small printed cards.
wrong: Cards is a sport played with a ball.

words.meaning: To become a member of a group.
wrong: I joined the club, so I left it.

words.meaning: To practice a sport to get better.
wrong: He trains hard, so he never practices.

words.meaning: To look at something for a time.
wrong: I watch the radio.

words.meaning: A picture made with a pencil or pen.
examples: Her {drawing} of a horse is very good.
wrong: A drawing is a song you sing.
